_comment: General, PUBLIC, category-level recognition reference keyed to taxonomy object_type values plus additional browsable categories. For analyst / first-responder recognition and cataloguing ONLY. NOT positive identification, and NOT fuzing, arming, render-safe, emplacement or defeat guidance. Figures are approximate and vary by model/manufacturer.
_disclaimer: General public reference for recognition and cataloguing — not identification, and not device-handling or render-safe guidance. Do not approach suspected munitions; cordon and contact EOD / the relevant authority.

mortar_round.label: Mortar round (generic)
mortar_round.summary: A finned, drop-fired projectile for indirect high-angle fire, spanning light (60 mm), medium (81/82 mm) and heavy (120 mm) families. As an unexploded item it is highly dangerous and may remain armed.
specs: Streamlined shell with tail fins; nose fuze common
ammunition: High-explosive (HE) — fragmentation against personnel and light targets
deployment: Fired from a tube with baseplate and bipod; towed, man-portable or vehicle-mounted
Encountered as UXO where a round failed to function
mortar_round.responder_note: Treat any suspected mortar round as live and potentially armed. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

mortar_60mm.label: 60 mm mortar round
mortar_60mm.summary: The light company/platoon mortar class — short-ranged, man-portable, used for close indirect support. Small but a serious hazard as UXO.
ammunition: High-explosive (HE) — fragmentation against personnel and light targets
deployment: Man-portable light mortar
Encountered as UXO
mortar_60mm.responder_note: Small size does not mean safe. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

mortar_81mm.label: 81 mm mortar round
mortar_81mm.summary: A widely fielded medium mortar class giving battalion-level indirect fire, heavier and longer-ranged than the 60 mm.
ammunition: High-explosive (HE) — fragmentation against personnel and light targets
deployment: Tube with baseplate and bipod
Encountered as UXO
mortar_81mm.responder_note: Assume live and potentially armed. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

mortar_82mm.label: 82 mm mortar round
mortar_82mm.summary: The Eastern-pattern counterpart to the 81 mm medium mortar, very common in many conflict zones. Frequently seen as UXO.
ammunition: High-explosive (HE) — fragmentation against personnel and light targets
deployment: Tube with baseplate and bipod
Encountered as UXO
mortar_82mm.responder_note: Assume live and potentially armed. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

mortar_120mm.label: 120 mm mortar round
mortar_120mm.summary: The heavy mortar class, bridging light mortars and towed artillery, delivering heavy indirect fire over several kilometres. Large explosive content.
ammunition: High-explosive (HE) — fragmentation against personnel and light targets
deployment: Towed or vehicle-mounted with a heavy baseplate
Encountered as UXO
mortar_120mm.responder_note: Large charge. Establish a wide cordon and contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rocket_generic.label: Rocket (unspecified calibre)
rocket_generic.summary: A rocket-propelled munition of unestablished calibre. Carries a motor plus a warhead; hazards include both the warhead and unburnt propellant.
deployment: Tube, rail or improvised launcher
rocket_generic.responder_note: Assume live warhead and propellant hazard. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rocket_107mm.label: 107 mm rocket
rocket_107mm.summary: A widely encountered light artillery rocket, spin- or fin-stabilised, fired from single tubes, light multi-tube launchers, or improvised single rails. Inaccurate individually and used for area effect.
deployment: Multi-tube launchers, single tubes, or improvised rails/ramps
Encountered as UXO or as a recovered intact round
rocket_107mm.responder_note: May contain an armed or damaged fuze and unburnt propellant. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rocket_122mm.label: 122 mm rocket
rocket_122mm.summary: A heavier artillery rocket associated with multiple-launch rocket systems, fin-stabilised, with greater range and warhead than the 107 mm class.
deployment: Multi-barrel launch systems, or improvised single launchers
rocket_122mm.responder_note: Large warhead and rocket motor. Cordon widely and contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rocket_240mm.label: 240 mm rocket
rocket_240mm.summary: A large-calibre heavy artillery rocket with a substantial warhead, used for area bombardment. Very hazardous as UXO.
deployment: Heavy multiple-rocket launchers or single launchers
rocket_240mm.responder_note: Very large warhead. Wide cordon; contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rocket_300mm.label: 300 mm rocket
rocket_300mm.summary: A very large heavy artillery rocket associated with long-range multiple-launch systems; may be guided in modern variants.
deployment: Long-range multiple-rocket launch systems
rocket_300mm.responder_note: Very large warhead. Wide cordon; contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_shell.label: Artillery shell / projectile (generic)
artillery_shell.summary: A gun-fired projectile across common calibres (roughly 105–155 mm and larger). Dense, robust body that often survives impact unexploded, making it a common and dangerous UXO and a frequent main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Thick steel, driving band near the base
ammunition: Base-bleed / extended-range and precision variants (some types)
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_shell.responder_note: High-hazard UXO; a fired-but-unexploded shell may be armed. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_105mm.label: 105 mm artillery projectile
artillery_105mm.summary: A 105 mm gun-launched indirect-fire projectile — a steel cylinder with a tapered nose, robust and dangerous as UXO. A common main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Steel, driving band near the base; nose or base fuze
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_105mm.responder_note: High-hazard UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_122mm.label: 122 mm artillery projectile
artillery_122mm.summary: A 122 mm gun-launched indirect-fire projectile — a steel cylinder with a tapered nose, robust and dangerous as UXO. A common main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Steel, driving band near the base; nose or base fuze
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_122mm.responder_note: High-hazard UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_130mm.summary: A 130 mm gun-launched indirect-fire projectile — a steel cylinder with a tapered nose, robust and dangerous as UXO. A common main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Steel, driving band near the base; nose or base fuze
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_130mm.responder_note: High-hazard UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_152mm.summary: A 152 mm gun-launched indirect-fire projectile — a steel cylinder with a tapered nose, robust and dangerous as UXO. A common main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Steel, driving band near the base; nose or base fuze
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_152mm.responder_note: High-hazard UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

artillery_155mm.label: 155 mm artillery projectile
artillery_155mm.summary: A 155 mm gun-launched indirect-fire projectile — a steel cylinder with a tapered nose, robust and dangerous as UXO. A common main charge in improvised devices.
specs: Steel, driving band near the base; nose or base fuze
deployment: Fired from towed or self-propelled guns
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
artillery_155mm.responder_note: High-hazard UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

tank_gun_projectile.label: Tank-gun projectile
tank_gun_projectile.summary: A high-velocity projectile fired from a tank main gun. Encountered as UXO or a recovered round; robust and dangerous.
deployment: Fired from armoured-vehicle main guns
tank_gun_projectile.responder_note: Treat as live UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

recoilless_munition.label: Recoilless / shoulder-launched munition
recoilless_munition.summary: A projectile fired from a recoilless rifle or shoulder-launched tube, common in man-portable anti-armour and support roles.
deployment: Fired from a tube or recoilless rifle
recoilless_munition.responder_note: Assume live warhead. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rpg_round.label: Rocket-propelled grenade (RPG) round
rpg_round.summary: A shoulder-launched rocket-boosted projectile widely used against vehicles and structures. Very common; a downed or dud round is a serious hazard.
deployment: Launched from a shoulder tube
Encountered as UXO or recovered rounds
rpg_round.responder_note: A dud RPG round may have an armed warhead. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

grenade.label: Grenade (generic)
grenade.summary: A small hand- or launcher-fired munition producing blast and fragmentation over a short radius. Small size but a serious close-range hazard and a common UXO.
specs: Hand grenade; 40 mm and rifle grenades
Blast and fragmentation, short lethal radius
deployment: Hand-thrown or launcher-fired
grenade.responder_note: A grenade with the safety lever released, or any UXO grenade, is extremely dangerous. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

hand_grenade.label: Hand grenade
hand_grenade.summary: A hand-thrown grenade using a lever-and-pin fuze. If the lever has separated, treat it as an immediate, extreme hazard.
deployment: Hand-thrown
hand_grenade.responder_note: If the safety lever is released, do not go near it. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

rifle_grenade.label: Rifle grenade
rifle_grenade.summary: A grenade launched from the muzzle of a rifle for greater range than a thrown grenade. Encountered as UXO.
deployment: Launched from a rifle muzzle
rifle_grenade.responder_note: Assume live. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

grenade_40mm.label: 40 mm grenade
grenade_40mm.summary: A launcher-fired low-velocity or high-velocity grenade, from single-shot launchers or automatic grenade launchers. Small, easily overlooked, and dangerous as UXO.
specs: Under-barrel or stand-alone launcher; automatic launchers
deployment: Launcher-fired
grenade_40mm.responder_note: Small and easily missed; still a live hazard. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

landmine.label: Landmine (generic)
landmine.summary: A victim- or command-initiated munition emplaced on or under the ground, in anti-personnel and anti-vehicle types. Designed to remain functional for long periods, making legacy and abandoned mines a persistent civilian hazard.
deployment: Surface-laid or buried; may be part of a marked or unmarked minefield
landmine.responder_note: Never approach, probe or move a suspected mine. Stop, retrace your steps, mark from a distance if safe, and contact mine action / EOD.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

anti_personnel_mine.label: Anti-personnel mine
anti_personnel_mine.summary: A mine designed to injure or kill people, typically small and triggered by pressure or a tripwire. A leading cause of civilian casualties long after conflicts end.
deployment: Surface-laid or buried, singly or in patterns
anti_personnel_mine.responder_note: Extremely sensitive. Do not move. Retrace your steps and contact mine action.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

anti_vehicle_mine.label: Anti-vehicle / anti-tank mine
anti_vehicle_mine.summary: A larger mine designed to disable or destroy vehicles, usually needing greater pressure to initiate. Contains a large charge.
deployment: Buried or surface-laid on routes and tracks
anti_vehicle_mine.responder_note: Large charge. Do not approach. Cordon and contact mine action / EOD.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

submunition.label: Submunition / bomblet
submunition.summary: A small munition dispensed in quantity from a cargo shell, rocket or air dispenser. High failure rates leave many unexploded and highly sensitive — a leading cause of post-conflict casualties.
specs: Dispensed from cargo rounds, rockets or dispensers
deployment: Scattered over an area from a carrier munition
submunition.responder_note: Extremely sensitive. Do not touch or go near. Mark from a safe distance and contact EOD / mine action urgently.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

cluster_munition.label: Cluster munition (carrier)
cluster_munition.summary: A carrier shell, bomb or rocket that opens in flight to scatter many submunitions over an area. The hazard is both the carrier and the many bomblets it leaves behind.
deployment: Dispenses submunitions over an area
cluster_munition.responder_note: Assume unexploded submunitions are present across a wide area. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

air_delivered_bomb.label: Air-delivered bomb (generic)
air_delivered_bomb.summary: A bomb released from an aircraft, from small to very large calibres, guided or unguided. Failed aircraft bombs are among the most hazardous UXO due to their large explosive content.
specs: Small practice to large general-purpose bombs (up to ~2,000 kg)
deployment: Released from aircraft
air_delivered_bomb.responder_note: Potentially very large charge. Establish a wide cordon and contact EOD immediately.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

general_purpose_bomb.label: General-purpose bomb
general_purpose_bomb.summary: The standard unguided aircraft bomb (e.g. the 250 lb / 500 lb / 1,000 lb / 2,000 lb families), a thick steel case around a high-explosive fill.
deployment: Released from aircraft
general_purpose_bomb.responder_note: Large charge. Wide cordon; contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

guided_bomb.label: Guided bomb
guided_bomb.summary: A general-purpose bomb fitted with a guidance kit (e.g. satellite- or laser-guided) for precision. Same large charge; may carry additional battery/electronics hazards when downed.
deployment: Released from aircraft
guided_bomb.responder_note: Large charge. Wide cordon; contact EOD. Do not approach.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

missile_generic.label: Missile (unspecified)
missile_generic.summary: A guided munition of unestablished type. Carries a warhead and propulsion; treat as extremely hazardous pending specialist assessment.
deployment: Ground-, air- or vehicle-launched
missile_generic.responder_note: Assume live warhead and propellant. Cordon widely and contact EOD.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

atgm.label: Anti-tank guided missile (ATGM)
atgm.summary: A guided anti-armour missile, often man-portable or vehicle-mounted, with a shaped- or tandem-charge warhead. A fired-but-unexploded round is very dangerous.
deployment: Man-portable, vehicle- or aircraft-launched
atgm.responder_note: Assume live warhead. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

manpads_missile.label: MANPADS missile (man-portable air-defence)
manpads_missile.summary: A shoulder-launched surface-to-air guided missile. A downed or dud unit carries a warhead and propulsion hazards.
deployment: Shoulder-launched at aircraft
manpads_missile.responder_note: Assume live warhead and propellant. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

loitering_munition.label: Loitering munition
loitering_munition.summary: A one-way attack munition that loiters over an area before striking, blurring the line between drone and missile. A failed or downed unit carries an intact warhead and battery/propulsion hazards.
deployment: Launched to loiter then strike a target
loitering_munition.responder_note: A downed or failed unit may carry a live warhead. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

one_way_attack_uav.label: One-way attack UAV / FPV munition
one_way_attack_uav.summary: An uncrewed aircraft — from small first-person-view quadcopters to larger fixed-wing types — carrying an explosive payload to a target. A crashed or dud unit is a live hazard.
deployment: Flown to a target and detonated on impact
one_way_attack_uav.responder_note: A crashed or failed unit may carry a live charge and battery hazard. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Wikipedia, Open Source Munitions Portal

improvised_explosive_device.label: Improvised explosive device (IED) — awareness
improvised_explosive_device.summary: A device made or placed in an improvised manner incorporating explosive material, in many forms and disguises. Recognition and avoidance only — no attempt at assessment or handling by non-specialists.
specs: Improvised; highly variable in form and initiation
deployment: Emplaced along routes, in vehicles, or in objects; may be disguised
improvised_explosive_device.responder_note: If an IED is suspected, do not approach or use radios/phones nearby unless locally advised. Cordon at distance and contact EOD.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

victim_operated_ied.label: Victim-operated IED (VOIED) — awareness
victim_operated_ied.summary: An IED initiated by the target's own action — for example stepping on a pressure device or disturbing a tripwire or an object. Functions like a landmine and is a severe civilian hazard. Awareness and avoidance only.
deployment: Emplaced where people or vehicles pass; may be hidden or disguised
victim_operated_ied.responder_note: Stop, do not move, retrace your steps if safe, and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

command_initiated_ied.label: Command-initiated IED — awareness
command_initiated_ied.summary: An IED set off deliberately by a person at a distance (by wire or remote signal) rather than by the victim. Awareness and avoidance only.
specs: Set off remotely by a person
deployment: Emplaced along routes; initiated when a target is in the kill zone
command_initiated_ied.responder_note: Treat any suspected device as live. Cordon at distance and contact EOD.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal, humanitarian mine-action guidance

projectile_generic.label: Projectile (unspecified)
projectile_generic.summary: A gun- or launcher-fired projectile whose precise type is not established. Treated as potential UXO pending specialist assessment.
deployment: Gun- or launcher-fired
projectile_generic.responder_note: Treat as live UXO. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal

uxo_generic.label: Unexploded ordnance (unspecified)
uxo_generic.summary: Any munition that was fired, dropped, launched or emplaced and failed to function, now posing a hazard. Type not established; treated as live pending assessment.
deployment: Varies
uxo_generic.responder_note: Assume it is armed and unstable. Do not touch, move or approach. Cordon and contact EOD / mine action.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal

small_arms_ammunition.label: Small-arms ammunition
small_arms_ammunition.summary: Cartridges for rifles, pistols and machine guns. Individually far less hazardous than explosive ordnance, but dangerous in fire or if mishandled, and often found alongside more serious items.
deployment: Found loose, in belts, or in containers
small_arms_ammunition.responder_note: Do not handle or place in fire. Report alongside any explosive items found nearby.
sources: Public references: Open Source Munitions Portal
